name: Serbia
summary_text: Serbia is a dangerous destination for trans visitors despite no criminalisation. The most acute documented traveler-axis risk is police: in February 2024 the Interior Ministry began investigating officers who beat, tortured and sexually harassed two LGBT people during a Belgrade apartment raid. About 105 sexual-orientation/gender-identity-motivated incidents were recorded in 2024, a masked attacker smashed the Pride information centre's front in 2025, Pride marches require heavy police protection, and testosterone HRT supply-chain disruptions have been documented. Serbia is outside the Schengen area (border checks for foreign travellers), legal-gender-recognition reform has stalled (the Law on Gender Identity was not adopted), and the anti-discrimination law is weakly enforced — public institutions "make minimal effort." One mitigating factor is a Belgrade prison's trans-sensitive search policy, which lets trans women choose the search arrangement, though watchdogs flag training gaps. Serbia has a lesbian prime minister (Ana Brnabić), but stalled legislation and police brutality make that largely symbolic rather than substantive protection. Major-tourist Belgrade is "conditionally" manageable with situational awareness.

sources.title: Serbia Investigates Allegations of Police Assault on Two LGBT People | Balkan Insight
sources.claim_summary: BIRN/Balkan Insight (Feb 2024): Serbia investigates allegations of police assault on two LGBT people during a drugs raid on a Belgrade apartment - the Interior Ministry's internal control section referred the complaint (from Da se zna!) to the Prosecutor's Office.

sources.title: Annual Hate Crime Report “Transphobia and Homophobia in Serbia 2024” Presented - Da se zna
sources.claim_summary: Da se zna! (Sept 2025): presentation of the 8th annual report 'Transphobia and Homophobia in Serbia 2024' - 105 incidents motivated by homophobia and transphobia in 2024, the highest number since monitoring began; includes quantitative and qualitative analyses of hate speech, hate crimes and discrimination.

sources.title: Serbia | APT
sources.claim_summary: Association for the Prevention of Torture country page for Serbia: NPM overview (Protector of Citizens as Ombudsman, operational since 2011, cooperating with six CSOs) and links to the Serbia country report on detention safeguards.

sources.title: World Report 2025: Serbia/Kosovo | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW World Report 2025 Serbia/Kosovo chapter: intolerance and violence against LGBT people remained significant concerns in 2024, alongside attacks on journalists and a flawed asylum system (Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity section).

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025 (covering 2024) chapter on Serbia: trans people face testosterone supply shortages (Testosteron Depo); a publication analysed 70 instances of politicians' hate speech (April 2023-April 2024); the Pride Info Centre was attacked in January and announced closure in September after 20+ attacks since 2018, none properly sanctioned; a Zoomer survey found three-quarters of trans/non-binary people fear job interviews due to anticipated discrimination.

sources.title: For foreigners — Talas TIRV
sources.claim_summary: Talas (Serbian trans organisation) page for foreigners: practical guide to living and transitioning in Serbia - rights, medical access, hormone supply; discrimination based on trans identity is prohibited by law but not always abided; transphobic attacks in public spaces are rarely physical but prejudices are common; recommends avoiding prominent LGBTIQ symbols, large sports events (hooligans), and trusting instincts.
AP (Sep 2024): 'Pride march held in conservative Serbia under heavy police protection' — Belgrade Pride proceeds under a large police cordon amid past far-right threats and authorities' ambivalence.

US State Department 2018 Human Rights Report for Serbia: human-rights issues include government corruption, violence against journalists, and 'crimes including violence targeting Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, and Intersex (LGBTI) individuals'.

sources.title: Country Overviews | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: OutRight International: Serbia's anti-discrimination law adopted - the 2009 Law on Prohibition of Discrimination explicitly covering sexual orientation and gender identity, a regional milestone.
